{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ed2d4145f350a027821fef156b7646bbaa534ec30ebb342540e4f8689ee8df72","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Learner permit and Class C licensing","heading":"C — Learner permit and Class C licensing","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Learner permit and Class C licensing

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
A first-time applicant must obtain a learner permit before beginning to drive in Pennsylvania. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Obtaining a driver license requires passing vision, knowledge and road tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Form DL-180 remains valid for one year after the physical examination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
The physical examination for the learner application may occur no earlier than six months before the applicant turns 16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
An applicant must reach age 16 before applying for a non-commercial learner permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The health care provider must complete the reverse side of the DL-180 application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
An examiner who cannot determine whether the application meets medical standards may delay the permit and require further medical examinations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
A seriously impairing condition may require a dual control learner permit and instruction from a certified instructor. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
For an applicant younger than 18, DL-180TD must be completed by a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
If the adult providing consent cannot accompany the applicant, that adult must sign DL-180TD before a notary. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
Consent documentation requires proper identification and, when surnames differ, evidence of the relationship. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
Applicants older than 18 must provide two residency proofs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
The completed DL-180 application must be brought to the Driver License Center rather than mailed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A01
An applicant younger than 18 must also bring the completed DL-180TD consent form for testing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A01
Documents establishing birth date and identity must be originals because photocopies are not accepted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A01
The items required for the knowledge-test visit include the applicant's Social Security card. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A01
The applicant must bring the applicable fee and consult the application for accepted payment methods. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A01
The back of DL-180 lists acceptable birth-date identification and the fees. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A01
The Driver License Center tests vision if a health care provider or optometrist has not already done so. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A01
Applicants who use corrective lenses should bring their glasses or contact lenses to the test visit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
After the knowledge test is passed, the examiner issues a learner permit valid for one year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
Driving practice may begin when the learner permit has been received. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
PennDOT recommends that young drivers book the road test when they receive the permit, with a test date no earlier than the permit's eligibility date. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
Before a road test, an applicant younger than 18 needs at least 65 hours of driving practice behind the wheel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A02
For applicants younger than 18, the required driving practice includes at least 10 hours at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A02
For applicants younger than 18, the required driving practice includes at least five hours in bad weather. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A02
A learner must always have a licensed supervisor in the front seat who is at least 21, or a licensed parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, or spouse aged at least 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A02
A driver younger than 18 must not carry more passengers than the vehicle has seat belts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A02
A young learner must wait six months after permit issue and have signed certification of the required 65 practice hours, including at least 10 at night and five in bad weather, before the road test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A02
An expired learner permit or three unsuccessful road tests can lead to using DL-31 to add, extend, replace, change or correct the non-commercial permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A02
Before using a Pennsylvania learner permit in another state, check its validity with the insurer and that state's transportation department. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A02
An applicant correcting permit information should bring supporting proof to the examiner at the testing visit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A02
Only one knowledge-test attempt is permitted in a day, even when the testing location changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A02
After a failed knowledge test, retain the returned application and consent forms because they must be brought to the next test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

Misconceptions: a learner permit and a junior license have different supervision rules; a birthday alone does not meet every road-test prerequisite.
Mnemonics: match the credential, the driver and the supervising adult before checking the driving restriction.
Glossary: learner permit means the credential used for supervised practice; junior license means the license carrying youth restrictions; consent identifies the adult authorization required for a minor applicant.
